reading.body:
Mike Quigley's AI record is dominated by data center siting, energy costs, and frontier model oversight, not by AI safety or research policy.

Eight of the thirteen events are cosponsorships, and six of those eight concern where data centers go or what they do to electricity rates and the environment. The Responsible Data Center Siting Act, the AI Data Center Site Selection Transparency Act, the Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act, the Power for the People Act, the SHIELD Act, and the Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act all sit in that cluster. The remaining two cosponsorships, the FRONTIER Act and the GUARDRAILS Act, address frontier risk reporting and state AI law preemption. The four recorded votes are on suspension motions, which the data does not describe beyond the motion and the yea vote.

The pattern matters because it locates the political pressure of AI in buildings and power rather than in model behavior. Siting, ratepayer cost, and environmental review are the subjects a member can legislate on with existing authority, and they are the subjects that appear here repeatedly across nine months. The single contribution entry, $2,500 from an Amazon segregated fund in May 2025, is the only money in the record and is too small and too isolated to support any inference about influence.

What the data does not cover is large. It holds no committee assignments, no hearing participation, no statements, no district-level data center projects, and no votes beyond four suspension motions. It cannot show whether these bills advanced, whether Quigley led or followed on any of them, or how he weighs data center growth against the electricity supply it requires. The dates are bill status dates, not introduction dates, so the sequence reflects when each measure last moved rather than when it was first filed.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Mike Quigley: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 13 events.
